title: Vividly Fermented Kenyan Bread Toast
description: A traditional Kenyan dish featuring crusty bread, fermented to perfection, and cut into thin strips using the katsuramuki technique, making it a nostalgic and jain-friendly option.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the water, sugar, and yeast, and let it sit for 5 minutes until the yeast is activated.
Add the salt, and 2 cups of flour to the bowl, and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it ferment in a warm place for 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
Punch down the dough, and shape it into a round loaf.
Place the loaf on a baking sheet, and bake for 25 minutes until it is golden brown.
Let the bread cool for 10 minutes before slicing it into thin strips using the katsuramuki technique.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat, and toast the bread strips until they are crispy and golden brown.
Sprinkle the chili flakes over the toast if desired.
Serve the vividly fermented Kenyan bread toast warm.
